A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fed-SB. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite reformatting and additional material in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning accuracy results for commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning and private natural language inference, including centralized and federated experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments on data heterogeneity, heterogeneous adapter ranks, rank sensitivity, memory use and training overhead.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds a rank-heterogeneous variant using a shared singular-vector basis, client-specific truncation and zero-padding of R before aggregation. This extends the procedure while retaining the original homogeneous BRA parameterization and averaging rule. The expanded initialization description documents an already-used strategy.

E1.justification: The datasets and task families remain unchanged. Section 4.1 adds a distinct extreme non-IID scenario in which eight clients each receive a different commonsense dataset, extending coverage to clients with separated data distributions.

E2.justification: Corresponding federated comparisons retain FedIT, FFA-LoRA, FedEx-LoRA and FLoRA; centralized private comparisons retain LoRA and FFA-LoRA. The added cross-method experiments reuse these comparators.

E3.justification: The original hyperparameter settings are retained, but the evaluation design expands substantially. New protocols include eight dataset-specific clients, heterogeneous ranks matched by aggregate squared-rank budget, arithmetic rank sweeps spanning 32–240, centralized private ranks spanning 16–80, and peak-memory and per-client training-time measurements.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's selected-rank comparisons, v2 adds robustness tests for extreme data heterogeneity and unequal client ranks, broader rank sensitivity studies, and analyses of memory consumption and initialization overhead. Table 3 and Appendices D–F investigate practical questions previously untested.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages from three independent runs. Neither reports confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests or additional uncertainty estimation; the retained plots also have unchanged uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original numerical results are unchanged: v1 Tables 2–5 correspond to v2 Tables 2, 4–6. Substantial new entries in Tables 3 and 7–11 report heterogeneity results, additional ranks and resource measurements. For example, Table 7 reports average accuracies of 75.52 and 75.89 for heterogeneous and homogeneous configurations at the matched 120-rank budget.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds formal definitions of local-rank subspaces and padded aggregation, with an exactness argument. The original homogeneous aggregation derivation and Lemma 1 proof remain unchanged. The newly written adapter slice axes conflict with the A and B dimensions specified in Section 2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of exact aggregation, client-count-independent communication per update, privacy advantages and state-of-the-art performance with up to 230-fold communication savings. Changes between Pareto-frontier and state-of-the-art wording do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning initialization, heterogeneous-rank robustness and rank/resource tradeoffs, including acknowledgment that optimal rank selection remains unresolved. It removes v1's limitations and future-work discussion. New experiments address the rank and data heterogeneity gaps, but the absence of vision-model evaluation is no longer acknowledged.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly explains initialization through averaged first-step updates, truncated SVD and layerwise computation. V2 also provides heterogeneous rank assignments and resource measurements. The 0.1% initialization sample fraction, hardware, original hyperparameters, precision settings and public code link were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion are retained, including positioning against LoRA-SB, FedEx-LoRA, FLoRA, FFA-LoRA and HetLoRA. Numbered citations and bibliographic formatting replace author–year presentation without adding research sources.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are preserved, with localized rewrites and expanded explanations. V2 adds an appendix contents list, organizes the additional material into dedicated sections, removes the limitations/future-work passages and adds an LLM writing-assistance disclosure.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column format with a single-column layout, substantially reflowing text, equations and displays. It adds six tables, revises table captions and placement, and rescales or relocates existing figures. All six figure contents are retained without substantive graphical changes.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful evidence on heterogeneity, rank sensitivity and actual resource costs, while explaining initialization more clearly. These address gaps in v1, but the net gain is limited by removing still-relevant limitations and introducing inconsistencies. For example, Table 3's Fed-SB rank-200 scores average approximately 75.09 rather than the reported 75.21, and Appendix D's adapter slicing conflicts with the stated matrix dimensions.
